description:
Making Beautiful Gelato with Costco Salted Caramel Sauce! 🥄✨

Can you turn Costco’s Salted Caramel Sauce into rich, creamy, luxury gelato? 🤔 We’re putting this popular caramel to the test, crafting a decadent homemade gelato that’s smooth, buttery, and packed with that perfect balance of sweet & salty goodness! Plus we are doing it in the Ninja Creami. 

---------------

225g Salted Caramel Butter Stuff from Costco
600g Milk (2% (semi skimmed) or Whole is fine)
250g cream 33% (34 or 36% is fine, Double Cream would make it even better!
)
30g SMP

7.5% fat, 20% sugars, 9.1% MSNF, 37% solids, 64% water

Serving temp -14°C / 6.8°F

-------------------

🔥 Timestamps:
0:00 – Introduction 🍦
0:15 – Ingredients in Costco Salted Caramel Sauce Breakdown 🛒
1:44 – Preparing the Gelato Base 🥛
3:11 – Spiny Spin Spin ❄️
3:56 – Dish Up and Fancy shots ⚙️
4:16 – Taste Test & Final Verdict! 🤤

If you love artisan ice cream, gelato science, or just want an excuse to eat more caramel, this video is for you! Don’t forget to like, subscribe, and hit the bell 🔔 for more next-level frozen treats!

comments.text:
Good evening Nick, I have a question unrelated to this gelato, hope you don't mind me asking. I've learn so much different ice-creams and gelato's because of your channel,

I'm currently using next to your channel the "Ice Cream Calculator"-app because it helps me make better ice cream and gelato that suits my taste while still being stable. Now I wonder why with chocolate and nuts gelato and Ice cream milk fat can be lower and milk solids don't seem to matter, while with other gelato and ice-cream recipes they do matter, so why can milkfat be lower with nutty Ice cream like Pistachio? And can i fully ignore the amount of milksolids in the ice cream?

And also it seems that my ice cream doesn't look as luxuries as the ones you produce, it doesn't even come close, I was wondering if this could be because I put too little ice-cream base in my icecreammaker? I have a Domo I cream maker with compressor that can make 2L Ice cream and many times I produce around 400ml of Ice cream. Or is this the difference between owning a Domo or a Musso 4080?

And thanks again for your channel and learning me a lot about Ice cream making, many thanks Kevin.
comments.author: @KevinVKleef

comments.text:
You can’t ignore the milk fat/ solids when doing any recipe but the solids type in nuts creates a unique texture that works with lower fat contents. 
Too little for the dasher to be effective. In a 2L machine you’d need to add 1.2-1.3L of base to achieve proper churn and overrun.
